name: Acme India Industries
lm_rationale: Hem Securities — 12 SME IPOs in 2026, 10 positive listings (83%), +30.34% avg listing-day gain (chittorgarh 2026 SME tracker); 2025: 16 issues, 88% positive, +20.96%.
fund_use_text: Mixed (debt repayment ₹41.00 Cr of ₹85.27 Cr itemised, plus ₹15.71 Cr OFS)
net_proceeds: Of the fresh issue, ₹38.00 Cr goes to working capital, ₹41.00 Cr to repay or prepay borrowings and ₹6.27 Cr to additional plant and machinery, with the balance to general corporate purposes. The ₹15.71 Cr OFS goes to promoter Suraj Pandey.
key_risks: The RHP says the business is entirely dependent on Indian Railways policy, and FY26 operating cash flow was negative at ₹(11.50) Cr as trade receivables rose to ₹252.18 Cr against ₹263.71 Cr of revenue.
market_moat: Since 2017 the company has completed 28 turnkey furnishing projects covering 1,610 coaches, and its Vande Bharat sleeper interior mock-up was accepted by the Railway Board in 2023. The RHP states there are no listed companies in India with a similar business.
management: Promoters Suraj Pandey and Sadhvi Pandey; 88.19% pre-issue promoter holding drops to 64.46% post-issue.
prose_business: Acme India designs, makes and fits railway coach interiors: turnkey furnishing of new coaches, refurbishment and conversion of old coaches, and toilet upgrades, plus supply of FRP parts, seats, berths, doors, epoxy flooring and Braille signage. It works through IREPS tenders across 16 railway zones from a Sonipat, Haryana facility. Indian Railways was 46.77% of FY26 revenue, down from 91.54% in FY25, as supply to private clients grew.
highlight_dev: Order book of ₹737.97 Cr across 40 orders as of 30 June 2026, 2.80x FY26 revenue from operations, of which toilet upgradation is ₹346.28 Cr and supply to private clients ₹229.09 Cr.
sector_outlook: The RHP's industry section puts the annual refurbishment market at ₹2,576 crore (8,588 coaches a year at ₹30 lakh each) and Indian Railways' FY 2025-26 rolling stock allocation at INR 589 Bn.
gov_scheme: The RHP sizes its refurbishment market off Indian Railways' Mission Retrofitment, at ₹30 lakh per coach.
peer_sentence: The RHP discloses no peer comparison, stating there are no listed companies in India engaged in a similar business, so the 18.89x post-issue P/E cannot be benchmarked against a document peer set.
verdict_reason: 18.89x post-issue P/E and 3.27x P/BV are fair, but FY26 operating cash flow was negative and receivables are 95.63% of revenue
why: FY26 revenue from operations rose 25.58% to ₹263.71 Cr and PAT 48.01% to ₹24.36 Cr, after a flat FY25, with D/E down to 0.82. At ₹196 the issue is priced at 18.89x post-issue EPS and 3.27x FY26 NAV, fair for a tender-driven railway supplier with no listed peer to compare against. Only ₹44.27 Cr of the ₹85.27 Cr itemised fresh proceeds goes to working capital and capex; ₹41.00 Cr repays debt and ₹15.71 Cr is promoter OFS. Hem Securities has a strong 2026 SME listing record (83% positive, +30.34% average). The main risk is cash conversion: FY26 operating cash flow was ₹(11.50) Cr with receivables of ₹252.18 Cr, and contingent liabilities stood at ₹92.98 Cr.
suggestion: Watch; apply only for listing on Hem Securities' record, and wait for subscription and GMP before committing. Cash conversion is the weak point.
